root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking something away wholly or in large part, especially by sweeping, scraping, or scooping.
root_idea.development: This basic idea extends to land eroded by water, torrents that carry things away, destructive forces, and figurative descriptions of voraciousness or loss.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested noun displayed under its normalized classical citation form.

senses.definition: An abrupt bank or ridge beside a valley or watercourse whose lower part has been eaten away by water, leaving it hollowed, undermined, and liable to collapse.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction على شفا جرف هار, it denotes the unstable, eroded bank at whose edge something is situated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To carry away, remove, or sweep away the whole of something, or much of it; of torrents, to erode or carry away land, and figuratively, to destroy people or livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used for physical removal and for a sweeping destructive force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To scoop, shovel, or sweep away dry material such as flour or sand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A use involving removal with the hands or a scooping action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be eaten up or consumed utterly, especially of herbage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Passive usage describing complete consumption of vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy or exterminate someone’s property or livestock and reduce the person to poverty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially said of time, fortune, misfortune, or calamities acting destructively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a place, to be invaded or overwhelmed by a torrent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction describes the place affected by the torrent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A smooth side or face of a mountain.
A torrent that carries away everything in its path; by extension, rain of such overwhelming copiousness.
A voracious person who devours food and leaves nothing remaining.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage based on the sweeping action of a torrent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who marries much or often and is brisk, lively, or active.
A sword that sweeps away everything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative description of the sword’s destructive effectiveness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large measure of capacity.
A capacious bucket.
A widespread destructive force, especially a prevailing death or plague that sweeps away people or livestock; also an affliction or evil fortune that destroys a people or their livestock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage presenting calamity as a sweeping torrent.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A swift animal, especially a fast horse or ass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported application to a male ostrich is identified in the evidence as a mistranscription of another word.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Greedy or possessed of an excessive appetite for food.
An unfortunate man.
Fingers or fingertips that take a great deal of food.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of grasping or consuming much food.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A broom or implement for sweeping mud from the ground; also a shovel, hoe, or rake.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The implement sense includes later or colloquial applications to tools used for scraping, digging, or dragging material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man whose property or livestock has been destroyed or exterminated and who has consequently been reduced to poverty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of the result of destructive time, fortune, or misfortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lean or emaciated.
Having lost its general fatness; lean or emaciated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied in the evidence to a ram, a camel, or a person.
